nodes.label: Source-of-Truth Hierarchy
nodes.rationale: Explicitly marks a prior AI draft (or an AI-generated brand-voice file) as not authoritative, closing the failure where a hallucinated claim gets copied from one AI-generated file into the next, each copy looking more credible for having survived a previous pass.

nodes.label: Brand DNA Spec (toolkit template)
nodes.rationale: Structured fields cost real nuance ('feels fresh and vibrant' captures something a hex code never will), but a narrower spec an agent can check itself against beats a richer one only a person can interpret, because only one scales past a human review queue.

nodes.label: Messaging Pillar Spec
nodes.rationale: Almost every messaging-pillar template stops at support points and proof, leaving the actual failure mode uncovered: a true support point gets stretched by an AI system into an unapproved claim because nothing told it where the line was. The 'do not say' line closes that gap per pillar; capping at three or four pillars keeps the list something a human reviewer and an automated check can both hold in full.

nodes.label: Positioning Statement Template (seven slots)
nodes.rationale: A looser positioning brief invites a paragraph of adjectives because nothing forces a specific claim out of the writer. Seven named slots remove that latitude — each demands a fact, not a feeling, and a statement with a blank slot is visibly unfinished rather than vaguely unconvincing, which is what makes it something an AI system can load as a constraint rather than a mood board.

nodes.label: Experiment Design Checklist (pre-launch gate)
nodes.rationale: The hypothesis must name a number, not just a direction — only a hypothesis that can fail is actually being tested. nodes.label: ROMI Formula (Incremental Contribution Margin / Marketing Spend)
nodes.rationale: ROAS (gross revenue over spend, no incrementality or margin) is deliberately excluded from the reference set because it can't fail — a channel with terrible margins and zero incremental effect can still post a large ROAS. State the COGS assumption out loud and re-run the number at a band around it every time; the sensitivity check is what turns 'trust this number' into something a reader can audit.

nodes.label: Data Readiness Audit
nodes.rationale: Not every gap is a blocker: a field that's slightly stale doesn't deserve the same response as an object that structurally doesn't exist anywhere. Treating every gap as equally urgent trains a team to ignore the audit or stall a launch over something that was never going to matter.
